_comment: Contract v2 (2026-09-10) — the three things the envelope grew and the one refusal it learned to word honestly: `query.events`, a `withdraw` that may omit its destination, `patrol`/`screen` aimed at a NAMED PLACE (compiled to a ring route), and a place-vs-force refusal that says which it is. Every fixture here runs on one of the boards added with the contract, so the behaviour is measured against a world that has a departure zone / a battle log / neither, rather than against `basin` with a flag flipped. The TS suites execute `expected` and assert the dispatch; tools/nl-eval scores the MODEL against the same `expected`.

fixtures.name: "withdraw" with no destination — the nearest departure zone
fixtures.note: Chimera is selected and stands at (900,1100); West Departure Zone at (200,1000) is nearer than East at (3800,3000). The envelope carries NO target: picking the zone is the resolver's job, and a model that named one would be guessing at distances it cannot measure.

expected.say: Chimera Squad is pulling back to the nearest departure zone.

fixtures.name: "pull back" is the same order
"fall back" is the same order again
a NAMED squad gets ITS nearest zone, not the selection's
fixtures.note: Warhound stands at (2800,2800): East wins. The fixture cannot see which zone was chosen from the send shape alone — that is `nl-resolver.test.ts`'s job — but it does pin that the order goes to group 3 and not to the selected group 1.

fixtures.name: a destination the player NAMED is never overridden by a zone
fixtures.utterance: withdraw Chimera Squad to East Departure Zone

expected.say: Chimera Squad is withdrawing to East Departure Zone.

fixtures.name: no departure zone on the map — refuse by name, do not invent one
fixtures.note: `basin` marks no landmark matching DEPARTURE_NAME. The model still emits the targetless withdraw (it cannot know what the map marks); the RESOLVER is what refuses, and it says so in words that name the fix.

fixtures.name: "patrol Osprey Fen" — a named place becomes a ring route
fixtures.note: A sentence cannot draw a polyline. Before contract v2 this refused with "use the composer's map arm", which made 2 of the 11 advertised verbs unreachable from voice.

fixtures.name: "screen Northgate" — the other route verb, same rule
fixtures.note: A team-wide (`any`) subject on a standing verb compiles to a StandingOrder, not a GroupDirective: `groupId 0` is the compile table's condition-scoped subject and there is no group to direct. Pinned here because the two wire types reach completely different gadget handlers.

fixtures.name: a named squad on patrol

expected.say: Chimera Squad is patrolling Fallow Gate.

fixtures.name: a patrol with a radius — the ring is the painted circle
fixtures.utterance: patrol a wide circle around Randtown
fixtures.note: A team-wide (`any`) subject on a standing verb compiles to a StandingOrder, not a GroupDirective: `groupId 0` is the compile table's condition-scoped subject and there is no group to direct. Pinned here because the two wire types reach completely different gadget handlers.

fixtures.name: "AI, patrol Osprey Fen" is advice, not a route (D60)
fixtures.note: An AI-subject order compiles to guidance, which carries a target entity and has no OrderShape at all — so the verb:shape table's route-only rule does not apply to it. Getting this wrong refused a sentence the guidance path can carry perfectly well.

expected.say: Advising the AI to patrol Osprey Fen.

fixtures.name: "defend Kestrel Flight" — a force is not a place, and the refusal says which
fixtures.note: The old answer was "I don't know a place called 'Kestrel Flight'", which is false — the game knows it perfectly well — and sent the player checking their spelling instead of fixing the sentence.

saysLike: one of your forces, not a place

fixtures.name: the model may refuse a force-as-place in its own words instead
fixtures.note: Both halves of the contract are legal: the model can emit the order and let the resolver word the refusal, or refuse itself. What it must never do is quietly retarget the sentence at a place with a similar name.

actions.reason: "Ironback Platoon" is one of your forces, not a place — name where you want them to hold.

fixtures.name: "what's happening" — the events query, newest first
"what's happening at Slag Forge" — narrowed to one place
"what's happening there" — the model writes the RESOLVED place
fixtures.note: Slag Forge is the drilled panel. Rule 10: with a focus in context the model names what it read, never the pronoun. The OFFLINE producer emits "there" and `bindFocusReferences` binds it — both arrive at the same envelope, which is the whole point of the contract.

fixtures.name: "sitrep" is the same question
an EMPTY battle log answers "nothing yet" — it does not refuse
fixtures.note: An empty history and an absent port are different states and get different answers. Collapsing them would tell a player in a quiet minute that the game had stopped recording.

fixtures.name: an empty log, narrowed to a place, says so about that place
no battle log at all — refuse by name
fixtures.note: `basin` declares no `moments`, so the port is absent. LOS honesty: "nothing happened" would be a claim the client cannot make.

fixtures.name: events near a place the map does not have — refuse, do not widen
fixtures.note: Dropping the unknown `near` and answering the whole map would answer a different question.

fixtures.name: events is a QUERY — it never moves anything
a question and an order in one breath — the query first, then the move
fixtures.utterance: what's happening at Slag Forge, then get everyone to Northgate
fixtures.note: Two actions, in the order the sentence said them (§1). A reordered pair is a different plan: the answer is what the player is about to decide the move on.

expected.say: Checking Slag Forge, then moving on Northgate.

fixtures.name: withdraw with no zone AND no destination is one refusal, not two
